solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English outlaw, short fat chap and gangster

parts.note: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest

indicators.note: short says the word for the fat chap loses its final letter

parts.note: a lump is a heavy, lumbering fellow

explanation.surface: A list of three characters: an English outlaw, a little fat man and a mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a violent petty criminal, a synonym for a gangster.

clue.text: Sharp point in diving posture?

definitions.meaning: a spike or pointed tip, as on the old infantry weapon
the jackknife position with legs straight and body bent at the hips

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spearhead's point and a bent-at-the-hips position in diving.

clue.text: Black stuff? What's taken up for comfort

parts.note: soot is the black powder left by burning

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking 'what?'

explanation.surface: Asking what black material is lifted to bring someone relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone is to comfort or calm them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Condensed material useful for a sleeper?

definitions.text: Condensed material useful for a sleeper?

parts.words: Condensed material useful for a sleeper?
parts.note: a sleeper here is a spy lying dormant, and condensed material is a document photographed down to a tiny dot

explanation.walkthrough: The sleeper seems to be someone asleep, but it is a sleeper agent; the condensed material is text shrunk photographically to dot size.
explanation.definitionFit: A microdot is a photograph reduced to the size of a full stop, a classic spy's device for hiding documents.

clue.text: Source of trouble — or likely help to an angler?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a matter that, once opened, causes many problems
a tin of bait worms is literally useful when fishing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a complicated problem is also literally a tin holding fishing bait.

clue.text: Transparent material you might see through glasses reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: per means through and specs are glasses

explanation.surface: Suggesting a see-through substance one might look at through spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspex is a British trade name for clear acrylic plastic sheet, a transparent material.

clue.text: Watch fool cutting through heath

indicators.note: cutting through says one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a moor is open heathland
nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on an idiot who is crossing the heathland.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to watch or keep it under observation, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stronghold in front of castle with elaborate detail

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows
elaborate as in worked over, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A fortress described as standing before a castle in intricate detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' reads as an adjective describing the detail, but it is the signal to rearrange that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city, a direct synonym for a stronghold.

clue.text: Group's ties I treated as impressive

indicators.note: treated as in processed, so these letters are put through a change of order

parts.note: the word with its s counted as a letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band's neckties handled so as to look impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges GROUPS, TIES and I; the s of Group's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestigious means having high status and esteem, so impressive is a close synonym.

clue.text: Fiennes, perhaps, showing a drive to involve commercial enterprise

indicators.note: to involve says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street names
a business venture is a commercial undertaking

explanation.surface: Fiennes showing a business-minded push as he ventures out.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is a British explorer famous for polar expeditions; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranulph Fiennes is a famous explorer and record-breaking expedition leader, an example of a daring traveller.

clue.text: Get rid of duelling without judge

indicators.note: without says a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: to joust is to fight a mounted duel with lances

explanation.surface: Banning a duel from taking place when no referee is present.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing J from JOUST leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel or remove them, a synonym for getting rid of them.

clue.text: Copper unusually stern with son, showing abrupt manner

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: unusually says these letters appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A policeman unexpectedly harsh with a boy, behaving brusquely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal; 'unusually' rearranges STERN into RTNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtness is brusqueness of speech, the quality of an abrupt manner.

clue.text: Useful accessory for spring?

parts.note: spring suggests the season, but means bouncing upwards

explanation.walkthrough: Spring seems to be the season; it is the act of jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is sprung canvas apparatus used for leaping high into the air.

clue.text: Duke, one with property, in depressing experience

parts.note: an owner is someone who possesses property

explanation.surface: A propertied aristocrat going through a gloomy episode.
explanation.definitionFit: A downer is informal for something dispiriting, a depressing experience.

clue.text: Medical record? It's packed and subject to study

parts.note: a suitcase is something one packs
history is an academic subject

explanation.surface: A patient file described as full and worth examining.
explanation.definitionFit: A case history is the record of a patient's past illnesses and treatment kept by doctors.

clue.text: Conservationists in country terribly discontented as a whole

indicators.note: in says the conservation body goes inside the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Environmentalists in a nation who are deeply unhappy all together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like unhappy but means emptied, keeping T and Y of terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety means the whole of something, as in taken in its totality.

clue.text: Chicago, perhaps, characterised by bars?

definitions.meaning: Chicago is a Broadway show with songs, an example of a stage show
bars of music, so having melody and rhythm

explanation.walkthrough: Chicago looks like the city with its bars, but it is the Kander and Ebb stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a famous stage show with songs, and musical also describes anything made of melodic bars.

clue.text: Shapely design of box, etc?

parts.note: box is the evergreen shrub, clipped along with yew and privet into ornamental shapes

explanation.walkthrough: Box seems a container but is the hedging shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping shrubs such as box and yew into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Order to destroy book in church stand?

definitions.meaning: a command to mash a volume into pulp, read as two words
the raised enclosed platform from which a preacher speaks

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as 'pulp it', an instruction to pulp a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised stand from which a sermon is preached, which split in two also gives an order to pulp something.

clue.text: Devilish type with suspect roots, a charlatan

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not in their right order

explanation.surface: A mischievous sort of dubious origins exposed as a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be someone else, so is a fraud or charlatan.

clue.text: Fussy sort, somewhat stooped antiquarian

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fusspot pictured as a bent-backed collector of old things.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone overly concerned with minor details and rules, a fussy sort.

clue.text: Something that could be sugared in shop illegally

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something sweetened being sold in a shop under the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying about sugaring the pill, making something unpleasant easier to accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill can be sugar-coated to make it easier to swallow, hence the idiom sugar the pill.

clue.text: Some drinks run out by receptacle in tournament?

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: Drinks gone, a rubbish bin, and a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is run out when the wicket is broken before reaching the crease; scorecards print it as ro.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a competition in which every player meets every other in turn.

clue.text: Old boy, one lacking substance as music-maker

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: lacking substance means the word is emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A former pupil, a hollow sort of person, playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, so a maker of music.

clue.text: Publication chewed over Northern industrialist

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
ate means chewed and swallowed

explanation.surface: A magazine pored over by a businessman from the North.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy and powerful business figure, such as a leading industrialist.

clue.text: Principality with men and artillery

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, enlisted men
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British Army regiment

explanation.surface: A small state with its soldiers and its big guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' gives OR (other ranks), soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small Pyrenean state ruled by two co-princes, so a principality.
